title: Definition
text: $$\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$$ is the y-coordinate of the point on the circle that lies $$\frac{1}{6} th$$ of the way along the circumference corresponding to the angle measure $$\frac{\pi}{3}$$.\n##figure4.gif##

title: $$30-60-90$$ triangle
text: The absolute values of the coordinates of this angle are given by the legs of a triangle with angles of $$30$$, $$60$$, and $$90$$. The hypotenuse has length $$1$$. The x-coordinate length is $$\frac{1}{2}$$. The y-coordinate is obtained from the Pythagorean theorem: $$\sqrt{1^2-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$.\n##figure5.gif##

title: Coordinate
text: The point on the unit circle with angle $$\frac{\pi}{3}$$ is in the first quadrant. Thus, the y-coordinate is positive, so it is $$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$.\n##figure6.gif##
